Chapter 9: Navigating Challenges and Seasons of Doubt
Every journey of faith comes with its valleys, doesn’t it? There are moments when things feel heavy—when God seems far away, prayers feel like they’re just bouncing off the ceiling, or when suffering really tests what we believe. If you’ve ever found yourself in one of those seasons, you’re not alone. These tough times aren’t a sign you’ve failed—they’re actually an invitation to lean in, to trust deeper, and to build resilience.
So, how do you move through these challenging stretches?
Honestly, it starts with being real. It’s perfectly normal to have questions, to feel fear, or to get discouraged now and then. Think of it like being caught in a sudden storm on a hike. The key isn’t pretending the storm’s not there—it’s about finding shelter, and reaching out for support when you need it.
Here are a few simple strategies that can really help:
First, name what you’re feeling. Sometimes just saying out loud, “I’m struggling,” or writing it down in a journal, or praying about it, can bring a wave of relief.
Next, seek out support. Don’t be afraid to talk to a friend, a mentor, or maybe a counselor. Someone who can listen, offer encouragement, or just help you see things from a new angle.
And then, come back to what you know is true. Remind yourself of God’s character, those moments when you saw faithfulness in the past, and the bigger picture you’re a part of.
You might notice that spiritual practices—like prayer or reading—feel kind of dry during these seasons. That’s okay. The invitation is to keep going, even when it feels routine. Growth often happens quietly, beneath the surface, just like a seed pushing through the dark soil before it breaks into the light. Sometimes, it’s those small acts—showing up, asking for help, or choosing gratitude—that keep hope alive.
And remember to give yourself some grace. Faith isn’t supposed to be a straight line. There are going to be ups and downs. Doubt isn’t the enemy of faith—more often, it’s the doorway to understanding something deeper.
Community matters most when things get tough. Sometimes, when your own hope feels hard to hold, someone else can carry it for you. Sharing stories—about struggle and getting through it—reminds us that we’re not alone and can make a world of difference.
In the end, facing challenges and doubts is all part of the journey. They shape us, deepen our empathy, and prepare us for new growth ahead. The promise isn’t that we’ll never struggle, but that we’re never alone in it. God is right there, in the middle of it all.
